## Findings by module

### greenhouse-year-6

- **refined** (ch-002.txt): HSE (UK): plant protection products, including insecticides, fungicides, slug pellets and rooting powders, must be authorised before they can be sold or used in the UK, and a home gardener is legally responsible for using them correctly. Module 6's general callout that 'rules differ between countries' can now state the UK rule and point to HSE's garden database.
- **extended** (ch-005.txt): HSE: check the HSE garden database for products authorised for the plant or area; never buy more than a year's need; do not buy pesticides online or abroad until the database confirms they are legal in the UK, because using or storing an unauthorised product can lead to prosecution; products on a stored shelf that no longer appear on the database are probably no longer authorised and must be disposed of.
- **extended** (ch-007.txt): HSE: most garden products are authorised for amateur use and need no training; professional products have more complex labels and by law may only be used by trained people, so an untrained gardener should never use them; withdrawn products have a use-up period with an expiry date, shown on the database.
- **extended** (ch-006.txt): HSE on home-made remedies: physical barriers and own-use remedies such as beer traps or coffee grounds generally fall outside the regulations, because intended use is part of the legal definition (garlic sold as food needs no authorisation, garlic sold as an insecticide does); but home-made chemical remedies are not risk-free and supplying one to someone else may need authorisation.
- **extended** (ch-010.txt): HSE on use: always follow the label, which may require keeping children and pets out of treated areas and waiting a set time before eating treated fruit or vegetables; read the label before buying and before use; make up only what is needed that day and never add extra to make it stronger; wash hands when finished.
- **extended** (ch-011.txt): HSE on storage: keep products in their original containers, a legal requirement; store out of reach of children and pets; garden sheds and greenhouses are not ideal stores because they get very hot or cold; never keep left-over diluted solution. Relevant to a greenhouse grower who keeps sprays on the potting bench.
- **extended** (ch-012.txt): HSE on disposal: never pour pesticides, diluted or not, down a drain, sink or toilet; empty plastic and aerosol containers can now go in household recycling; ask the council about disposing of unwanted product; do not burn packaging.
- **note** (ch-003.txt): HSE asks gardeners to consider first whether control is necessary and whether there is a non-chemical alternative, such as hand removal or a physical barrier, pointing to the RHS, Garden Organic and RSPB. Matches the course's 'non-chemical first action' decision rule.

Totals: 0 confirmed, 1 refined, 0 contradicted, 6 extended, 0 absent, 1 note.
